headline: Dolly Parton’s Onetime Hollywood Hills Home Lists for the First Time in a Generation Asking $7.95M
author: Kanebridge

paragraphs.text: 95 million. 2 million, according to listing records. The property, aptly known as the Dolly Parton House, hasn’t been on the market for 25 years, according to the listing with Edward Tinney of Nourmand & Associates and Kurt Rappaport of Westside Estate Agency.

There's a library and media room. Paul Barnaby Photography It’s unlikely Parton and Dean would recognize the house as it stands today though; it was rebuilt in 2009, and upgraded further in the years since, the listing said. Across its almost 4,700 square feet, the house has living and dining rooms with walls of glass that frame the views that stretch across the city to the Pacific Ocean.

Paul Barnaby Photography There’s also a library and media room, a family room and an eat-in kitchen. There are four bedrooms, including the primary suite, which has a coffee bar, a fireplace, two bathrooms, a space for an office or gym, a walk-in closet and a private deck.

Outside, there’s a pool and spa, with space for outdoor dining and entertaining. Plus there’s a two-car garage, electrical infrastructure for an EV charger and a Zen trail, according to the listing. 05 million for the home in 2001, records with PropertyShark show.

Paul Barnaby Photography Parton died on August 25 at the age of 80 after a battle with cancer. She released 50 studio albums over the course of her career—resulting in 27 gold and platinum albums—and starred in films including “9 to 5,” “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas” and “Steel Magnolias.” A philanthropist, she was behind the Imagination Library, which donated more than 200 million books to children around the world.
In 2020, she helped fund early research for Moderna’s Covid 19 vaccine with a $1 million donation to Vanderbilt University.
